### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/vitest.repo-tests.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c7e7505271c32204e1d5918e7a3fe62822fc87d`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/vitest.repo-tests.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/data/{source} (route, 58 pages)`, `/data/{target} (route, 58 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **38** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c7e7505271c32204e1d5918e7a3fe62822fc87d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a24a290b5d5e041b981beb4c58e3bdf57728fa32` — the merge of head `d08c27bedf6fa74fc9255d4b630a9c3908ba3e0d` into base `7c7e7505271c32204e1d5918e7a3fe62822fc87d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a24a290b5d5e041b981beb4c58e3bdf57728fa32 && git checkout a24a290b5d5e041b981beb4c58e3bdf57728fa32
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7c7e7505271c32204e1d5918e7a3fe62822fc87d d08c27bedf6fa74fc9255d4b630a9c3908ba3e0d && git checkout -B drift-repro 7c7e7505271c32204e1d5918e7a3fe62822fc87d && git merge --no-ff d08c27bedf6fa74fc9255d4b630a9c3908ba3e0d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c7e7505271c32204e1d5918e7a3fe62822fc87d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7c7e7505271c32204e1d5918e7a3fe62822fc87d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d08c27bedf6fa74fc9255d4b630a9c3908ba3e0d`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #22661 (body; comments 6096329009 triage, 6101260211 claim, 6102815147 dev report), PR #22735 (body, its 12-file list, the net diff from merge-base `a360cee92e` to the head — 12 files, +1181/−5, byte-matching the file list), and the head's check-runs, read 2026-10-10T22:36Z. Of 32 check-runs: 13 concluded `success` (Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, filter, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · source gates), 3 `skipped` by their own triggers (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), and **16 still in progress** at the read (Build Core; Test Core 1–6; Dogfood Regression Gate 1–3; Dogfood Verify CLI; Lint & Repo Gates; Temporal Conformance; Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger). This record judges the diff and the concluded set only; the in-progress families conclude on their own and the owning seat reads them before arming — a red there is theirs to act on, not pre-judged here. Security card: classes, positions and functions only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — accept-set narrowing at `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.findData` and `getData`.** An expand entry whose TARGET object's declared exposure refuses `get` is withheld before the engine is called, at every level of the tree; the field answers its stored id; no response status changes. **Right.** One intake: read at the head, `rest-server.ts` hands the list, query and export routes to `findData` (the export door builds its relation map from `export-format.ts` and passes it the same way) and the single-record route to `getData`; the runtime dispatcher's `callData` reaches the same two members (`action-execution.ts`, `domains/data.ts`); the MCP package has no expand intake. The engine resolves the sub-read's object by `referenceTargetOf(fieldDef)` (`ObjectQL.expandRelatedRecords`), never by the entry's own `object` key, so the door judges the same object the engine would read — no spelling bypasses it. A nested `expand` in a non-map shape is left alone by `servedExpand` and read as nothing by `expandRelatedRecords` (it iterates object entries), so that guard's gap has no read behind it.
2. **Operation `get` on both doors (`EXPANSION_TARGET_OPERATION`, `LABEL_TARGET_OPERATION`).** **Right.** Both reads turn an id the caller holds into the record it names — the single-record route's read; the expansion sub-read is id-bounded, the label read is per-record. A `list`-only target is withheld, a `get`-only one served, identically on the data door and the dataset door; the relationship-hop dimension stays `aggregate` over `queryObjects`. A single operation across both doors is the one-rule shape the card requires; `aggregate` on the label face would have split the answer for the same target.
3. **Withheld, not refused.** **Right** — the card's own prescription and the measured precedent (an unreadable related record answers the bare foreign key from `expandRelatedRecords`; a row-scope-hidden label answers the raw id). No new error code, as the dispatch asked. The dogfood `PRECEDENT` leg pins the member-unreadable case unchanged, so the new answer is the old answer's shape.
4. **Placement at the door, engine untouched.** **Right.** `packages/objectql` is not in the file list; a flow's `config.expand` and a hook's own read keep their privileged path, the split #7823 and #22646 drew. The withhold runs after `assertExpandTargetsExist` and before the `internal: true` walk, so nothing about a withheld target is judged or named.
5. **One decision, no second rule.** `servesExpansionTarget` asks `canServeApiOperation`; `servesLabelTarget` asks `apiExposureDenialReason`. **Right**: `api-derivation.ts` defines the first as the boolean face of the second; the enumeration pin accepts either face and goes red when a decision function stops asking.
6. **Failure modes.** Depth backstop drops the entry (closed). The label face catches a throwing declaration provider and withholds at `warn` (closed; the query still answers). The expand door's registry read is unwrapped — a throw there fails the request (closed too). A null field gate (a legacy array field map) stands down exactly as the #22646 walk beside it does: inherited, named here, not new. **Right.**
7. **`AnalyticsService` constructor: the label resolver is wrapped by `withServedLabelTargets` only when `getObjectDeclaration` is wired; absent probe, no gate.** **Right, with the dependency named**: the stand-down is the query face's existing one-shot behaviour, the plugin (`plugin.ts`) wires the probe in production, and the dogfood pin exercises that real wiring. The per-request `withLabelFetchCache` wraps the served wrapper (line order read at the head), so a withheld target's empty map is cached per request only; `translateSelectOptions` passes through.
8. **Public surface.** `servesLabelTarget` (api-exposure-door.ts) and `withServedLabelTargets` (dimension-labels.ts) are module exports NOT re-exported by `index.ts`, which the diff leaves untouched; the protocol's new members are `private`. **No public widening — right.**
9. **Copy-on-write.** `findData` works on a shallow copy of the request's query; `servedExpand` copies only on change and returns an unchanged tree by reference; the caller's map is pinned unmutated. **Right.**
10. **Enumeration pin (`second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`, core `repo` project).** Every non-test caller of `referenceTargetOf` is classified; an unclassified caller, a stale classification, or a decided read whose decision function stops asking turns it red; it cannot pass vacuously (the prefilter and matcher are checked against every classified file and the arbiter's own declaration). The discriminator's blind spots are declared rather than discovered later (hop-object, the import door's raw reference carrier, fixed platform targets). **Right.** The `open` rows' carrier text will need the follow-up card numbers once filed (③).
11. **The ledger row (`engine-double-contract.pinned.json`) and the `vitest.repo-tests.json` entry** are the gates' own prescriptions for the new protocol double and the cross-package pin. **Right.**
12. **Reach claim** bounded to in-repo sources at `eae3368a`, deployed and cloud-held definitions declared NOT MEASURED. **Right** — the bound is stated, not hidden.
13. **Pins and ablations.** The protocol and analytics pins pair every withheld shape with a served control and assert on what the engine receives; the dogfood pin arms itself on each target's own single-record answer before believing any expansion or label, for both personas. The ablation ledger (A, B, B2, C, D1, D2) is the dev's measurement; nothing was re-run here (read-only brief). What this record judges is the pins' construction, which cannot pass with the decision bypassed, and the shapes they cover match the decision's whole distinction set for `get`.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `22661-second-object-exposure.md`: `minor` for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/service-analytics`**, with the `!` summary, the `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM → TO stated, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — no spec key, spelling, export or stored shape moves). **Right**: an accept-set narrowing is breaking and the launch window ships breaking as `minor` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`); `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head. The other touched packages publish nothing from this diff (core: a test and its vitest list; dogfood: a test and a fixture; scripts: a ledger row), so the two named packages are the whole publishing set.
- **`Clause-②: no`** on the PR body and the changeset. **Value right**: no widening — no new public export, no new error code, no accept set grows. **Arm absent while the diff IS a narrowing**: `no (narrowing)` is the spelling the arm exists for (`clause2-line.mjs`); an absent arm declares no direction, a reading the fleet's one reader tolerates by design, and breaking-ness reaches `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` through its `!` and banner signals, so no gate is blind to it. Judged a declaration gap copied verbatim from the dispatch's claim (dev deviation e), not a semver mismatch. Prescription, non-blocking: the owning seat edits the PR body's line to `no (narrowing)`; a body edit moves no head and spends nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: none** (the dev report's list is empty).
- **Deviation (a)** census rows 4–7 unfixed: **answered — by design**; the PR says `Part of`, the gate `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green, and row 4's answer (a refusal in the data door's codes plus a provenance row in `packages/spec`) is outside this claim's compile surface as the dispatch set it.
- **Deviation (b)** label face judged `get`: **answered — right** (①.2).
- **Deviation (c)** engine-double ledger row: **answered — right** (①.11).
- **Deviation (d)** dogfood pin, fixture and enumeration pin outside the two named packages: **answered — right**; each sits beside its sibling pin, and the dispatch named "the enumeration pin" without a package.
- **Deviation (e)** `Clause-②` copied verbatim: **answered in ②**, prescription given.
- **Deviation (f)** rate-limit wall on the first run: process note; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts — **no effect on this record**.
- **Deviation (g)** `origin/main` moved two commits (cli, lint) after the final merge: **answered — no re-merge owed**; the PR reads `mergeable` on current main and the queue leg re-merges on landing.
- **Four `class: a` out-of-scope findings (census rows 4–7)**: **escalated to the dispatching seat** — as of this read the card carries no filed sub-issue for any of them; each needs its card under #22661 (the dedupe words are in the dev report) so the enumeration pin's `open` carriers and this PR's `Part of` have somewhere to point. The filing is the seat's act, not this record's.
- **Carrier note (`import-field-meta.ts` reads the target off the raw reference carrier, not `referenceTargetOf`)**: **escalated** — recommend folding it into row 7's card rather than a separate filing: the import door's fix touches that site, and it is the reason the enumeration pin cannot see that door.
- **Check-runs in progress** (16, named above): the verdict stands on the diff and the concluded set; landing still waits on CI green per the Post-Task Checklist.
- **Governed surfaces**: none of the 12 paths hits a `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded `success`. This record is the contract-tier review the dispatch's narrowing asked for before the queue, not a Tier S landing record.
